spec.name: routing-by-name
spec.intent:
Census @a9258730; re-derive any line cited below if its path changed since (guards-skip-subagents lands first and edits packages/canon/src/hooks/stance-guardrail.ts, stance-guardrail-pre.ts and their targets). Realize in the stance rubric the act `architect role` prescribes: the architect starts a plan's work, and routes every verdict, by a unit's name alone; a unit's name is an address, not something it reads, and the spec at that address, which the planner wrote, carries the unit's distilled intent. A dispatch that routes a unit by name is therefore a substantive dispatch, not a dispatch echo.
AT CENSUS. The rubric's source is the `stance-judge-prompt.md` worker of packages/canon/src/hooks/stance-guardrail.ts (content from L1028; filename at L952), projected to packages/canon/targets/guardrail/stance-judge-prompt.md (13968 bytes) and read by both guards on both harnesses (omp's bridge reads the same file; it embeds no copy). Signal 4, Dispatch-echo (L1069-1071), blocks a dispatch that transcribes the operator's or a coordinator's literal words, 'or names sources and carries no distilled instruction'; the boundary test at L1116 passes only 'a distilled objective'. The rubric never says unit. At 2026-09-30T10:16:56Z the omp pre-call guard denied the architect's routing of guards-skip-subagents, omp-guards-skip-subagents and units-in-worktrees with 'This is a dispatch-echo: the prompt only points the delegate at a spec command and lists unit names'. That task call had context "Plan `loop-friction`, repository /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus. Your unit's spec: `cratylus plan show <unit> --plan loop-friction`." and three tasks whose text was "`guards-skip-subagents of loop-friction`", "`omp-guards-skip-subagents of loop-friction`" and "`units-in-worktrees of loop-friction`"; omp hands the worker an Agent call whose prompt is the context and each task text joined by a blank line. The purview guard already passes 'a dispatch routing a unit name to an implementer' and denies a dispatch carrying a spec the dispatcher wrote (packages/canon/src/hooks/purview-guardrail.ts:33-37), so today the two guards leave the architect no dispatch that passes both. The pre-call guard's deny notice lists as legitimate exceptions only a consent choice, an intent ambiguity and 'a substantive intent-extracted dispatch' (stance-guardrail-pre.ts:262-264; header L56-57 says the same). The calibration tool packages/canon/test/support/guardrail/calibrate-stance-judge.sh judges turn-*.txt fixtures as expected-BLOCK and controls/*.txt as must-PASS; no fixture or control is a dispatch. `claude -p` does not answer on this host under the user's settings (note 'claude -p never answers on this host under the user's settings'); the 2026-09-30 calibration used omp's advisor role through STANCE_JUDGE_CMD (expected.json `_cut_rubric`).
CHANGE. In the rubric, signal 4 and its boundary test say that a dispatch routing a unit of a named plan by its name (to be built, back to its builder with an assay's findings, to be assayed, or to be made whole), with at most where its spec is read, is a substantive dispatch and PASSes: the intent lives in the spec at that address. A dispatch pasting the operator's or a coordinator's literal words still BLOCKs. Keep the rubric within 14 KB, the size packages/forge/src/adapters/omp/render.ts and its test state the judge's time budget was measured against. The pre-call guard's header and deny notice name a unit routed by name among what it does not deny. Regenerate packages/canon/targets/guardrail with `pnpm canon:project:targets`. Add to packages/canon/test/fixtures/guardrail a must-PASS control controls/route-units-by-name.txt holding the `payload` that targets/guardrail/stance-guardrail-pre.sh emits under STANCE_EMIT_PAYLOAD for a main-session Agent call whose prompt is the denied routing above, and an expected-BLOCK fixture dispatch-echo.txt holding the payload the same worker emits for the hermetic suite's DISPATCH_ECHO prompt; make calibrate-stance-judge.sh judge dispatch-*.txt as expected-BLOCK beside turn-*.txt; record both in expected.json with the measurement and name them in the fixtures README. Add .changeset/routing-by-name.md (@cratylus/canon patch).
accept: `git grep -n -w -i unit -- packages/canon/targets/guardrail/stance-judge-prompt.md` prints a line of signal 4 (Dispatch-echo) and a line of the Boundary tests, each saying a dispatch that routes a unit of a named plan by its name PASSes. At a9258730 it prints nothing.

`git grep -n -i 'by name' -- packages/canon/targets/guardrail/stance-guardrail-pre.sh` prints the deny notice's line naming a unit routed by name among the calls it does not deny. At a9258730 it prints nothing.

packages/canon/test/fixtures/guardrail/controls/route-units-by-name.txt is byte-identical to the `.payload` that targets/guardrail/stance-guardrail-pre.sh emits under STANCE_EMIT_PAYLOAD for the main-session Agent call whose prompt is the denied routing of 2026-09-30T10:16:56Z; print the command that shows it (cmp exits 0). Judged 5 times each with STANCE_RUBRIC set to the rubric at a9258730 (`git show a9258730:packages/canon/targets/guardrail/stance-judge-prompt.md`), it is BLOCKed in at least 1 of 5; with the new rubric in 0 of 5. Print both tallies and the judge used.

`sh packages/canon/test/support/guardrail/calibrate-stance-judge.sh 5` against the new rubric, with STANCE_JUDGE_CMD naming the judge used above, prints a table in which dispatch-echo and each of the six turn fixtures is ok at 5/5 BLOCK and every control, route-units-by-name included, is 0/5 BLOCK; print the table. expected.json records these numbers and the judge.
After the commit, `pnpm canon:project:targets` leaves `git status --porcelain packages/canon/targets` empty.
Green: `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon exec vitest run test/stance-guardrail-dark.test.ts`, `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon run stance-guard:test` and `pnpm --filter @cratylus/canon typecheck` exit 0.
